The measured X1‑X2 resistance equals the sum of all three resistors (18.333 Ω). The measured N_b1‑X2 resistance equals R2 + R3 (13.333 Ω). To satisfy the note that one resistor is twice another, set R2 = 2 × R3. Solving gives R3 ≈ 4.444 Ω and R2 ≈ 8.889 Ω. This topology matches all measurements and the “one is twice another” condition.</thought>
